requirements.requirement: RabbitMQ cluster running across node1, node2, and node3
requirements.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status on node1 shows all three nodes (rabbit@node1/2/3) as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes both immediately after formation and again after the full restart sequence, corroborated by per-node listener output (5671/15672/25672 all up on each node).

requirements.requirement: A cluster-specific CA is created and used to issue certificates for the cluster
requirements.summary: A self-signed CA (CN=rabbitmq-cluster-CA) was generated with openssl, then used to sign per-node server certs (with correct SANs) and a client cert; a separate untrusted CA was created only for negative testing, not used for the cluster itself.

requirements.requirement: AMQP is served over TLS and only clients presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA are accepted
requirements.summary: rabbitmq.conf disables plaintext AMQP (listeners.tcp=none), enables AMQPS on 5671 with verify_peer/fail_if_no_peer_cert=true. Server logs show fatal TLS alerts rejecting a connection with no client cert (certificate_required) and one signed by an untrusted CA (Unknown CA). A real pika-based AMQP client using the CA-issued cert completed publish/consume from both node1 and node2, while the same flow using an untrusted-CA client cert failed with an SSL unknown_ca error, both before and after the restart sequence.

requirements.requirement: Management interface is reachable only from within the cluster
requirements.summary: firewalld/nft rules on all three nodes only accept 15672 (plus 25672 and 4369) from source 10.100.162.0/24, which is the cluster's own subnet containing exactly node1-3; all other sources fall to default deny. A cross-node HTTP call from node2 to node1's management API over the cluster network succeeded (200), confirming intra-cluster reachability; no external-source negative test was captured, so exposure to outside the /24 is not directly demonstrated, but the deny-by-default firewalld posture combined with the explicit rich rules is standard supporting evidence for this outcome.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node1: pre-restart baseline, ack, changed boot id, recovered state
requirements.summary: Boot id captured before (67c52137...) and reboot acknowledged via a closed exec stream; post-restart boot id changed to 3d43725e..., matching the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot exactly. Cluster status, listeners, and the durable queue message were all confirmed recovered afterward.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node2: pre-restart baseline, ack, changed boot id, recovered state
requirements.summary: Boot id captured before (555221a1...) and reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot id changed to 785331da..., matching the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot. Cluster status and AMQPS/management listeners confirmed up again after restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node3: pre-restart baseline, ack, changed boot id, recovered state
requirements.summary: Boot id captured before (34027437...) and reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot id changed to 35b6d70e..., matching the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot. Cluster status and listeners confirmed up again, and a final end-to-end check (durable message present, valid client works, untrusted client rejected) was run after all three restarts.

overall_summary: The executor stood up a functioning 3-node RabbitMQ cluster with mutual TLS enforced by a purpose-built CA, verified both positive (CA-issued client) and negative (no cert, foreign-CA cert) AMQP-over-TLS behavior via server logs and real pika client tests, and confirmed the management API is firewalled to the cluster's own subnet with a working intra-cluster access check. The mandatory node-restart protocol was completed for all three nodes with matching boot-id transitions cross-verified against the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and cluster/queue/TLS state was shown recovered after each restart and again after the full sequence. Minor hygiene deductions apply for unremoved temporary files left in /tmp across all three nodes.
limitations: No direct negative test was captured showing the management port is actually blocked from a source address outside the 10.100.162.0/24 cluster subnet; reachability was only confirmed from inside that subnet.

Selected evidence covers only a subset of the 96 total commands; a few early failed discovery commands were reviewed from the full timeline but the complete command set was not exhaustively cross-checked for anomalies beyond what the timeline surfaced.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to task outcomes: repo/package installs, CA/cert generation, cert distribution over SSH, rabbitmq.conf edits, plugin enablement, firewalld rules, test user/queue creation for durability proof, and the sequential reboots. Several early attempts to fetch a cloudsmith setup script returned 404s and one curl attempt (cmd-38ee2f8cf9c849a4) failed to write a file; these were read-only discovery/troubleshooting with no state mutation and are not penalized. Restarting sshd on node2 and node3 (cmd-8603048261744823, cmd-a742db6ebba4416c) was a necessary, bounded prerequisite to enable pubkey auth for the SSH-based cert distribution used later, and is reasonably tied to the material outcome. The main hygiene deduction is residual, unremoved temporary artifacts left in /tmp after the run (erl.sh, reboot.log, rmq_node2.conf, rmq_node3.conf on node1; reboot.log, rp1.log, rp2.log on node2/node3), visible in the after-executor vs. after-prepare temporary-files diff -- these are low-risk, non-sensitive leftovers (config snippets and install logs) that were never cleaned up, but they do not weaken any security control or conflict with services.
